description: ODC (coverage C): the data-action-reactive.json and data-action-entity-list-reactive.json of the O11 lane mirrored and together in the ODC lane. A DATA ACTION is the third data source of a screen (beside the Screen Aggregate and the input parameter): it fetches by LOGIC, runs on the server and returns whatever you want. Two screens prove the two halves. WfDaKpis: STRUCTURE List output, Fetch AtStart (the screen fetches by itself on opening) and OnAfterFetch linked to a screen action that stamps the time - the `get` shows that Fetch is a real property in the model, and not a silent default. WfDaRegions: ENTITY List output, and therefore Current exposes the attributes DIRECTLY (GetWfDaRegions.Regions.Current.Name, without the entity wrapper that an aggregate forces), Fetch OnDemand (the screen does NOT fetch on opening) and a Refresh Data on a button to trigger the fetch. The tenant census says that the 121 data actions of the real modules all have the Fetch property written: this job is the first in the lane to write it, in both values.

ops._why: the data action is born on the IMobileScreen itself (IMobileScreen.CreateDataAction), like the screen aggregate - not on the @espace

PLATFORM DIFFERENCE recorded: in ODC the IDataAction has the Fetch property (enum DataSourceFetch: AtStart | OnDemand) and it is already born as AtStart; writing it by hand is what closes the parity with the census, which sees the 121 real instances with Fetch defined
same as SS11: the data action is born with a sample output Out1; left as it is, it gives Error InvalidDataAction_OutputMustBeSet and Warning UnusedElement
the output of a data action does not need to be an entity: here it is the list of a structure, which no aggregate knows how to return

ops.name: CountRegions
ops._why: inside the data action the aggregate is a NODE (IAggregateNode), not the IScreenAggregate of the screen; and the name cannot be the default GetWfDaRegions, otherwise a future filter renames it and the expressions break

PLATFORM DIFFERENCE recorded: the SS11 job writes IActionSignature:ListAppend; in ODC the ListAppend exists as IClientActionSignature AND as IServerActionSignature, and the body of the data action runs on the SERVER - which is why it is the server signature that the IExecuteServerActionNode accepts
the layout applies to the flow of the data action as to any action
OnAfterFetch is an IUILifeCycleEvent of the IDataAction itself: it is read as a property that returns an object ($da/OnAfterFetch) and linked through the Destination, like the OnClick of a button
the source of the List is <DataAction>.<Output>, and it is THIS that gives the data action a consumer (without a consumer ODC gives Warning UnusedAction, like any action)
reads the variable that OnAfterFetch stamped: proves that the event runs after the fetch
the OTHER value of the enum: the screen opens WITHOUT fetching and waits for a Refresh Data; it is the difference that the `get` of the two data actions shows side by side
ENTITY List output: this is what changes the reading on the screen (Current without wrapper)

allowForEach.why: a proof job written before the owner rule reached raw ops: the loop copies the rows into a list (T2), kept as written and listed

ops._why: INSIDE the logic the aggregate line has the entity wrapper (.Current.WfDaRegion); it is the output typed as an entity that removes the wrapper on the SCREEN side - the two readings coexist in the same job on purpose
the Refresh Data points to the DATA ACTION (the DataSource is an IObject: it serves the screen aggregate and it serves the data action); it is the only way for an OnDemand data action to get to run

THE POINT OF THE SECOND HALF: with an ENTITY List output, .Current.Name is read directly. In an aggregate the same reading would be .List.Current.WfDaRegion.Name - the wrapper exists because the aggregate can join several sources, and the output of the data action cannot
